"How to be hungry and keep going anyway."
"The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration."
"Do go on."
"tracking. Sounds small. But small useful things stack — and one day you look up and you're the person everyone asks. That's how it happens. Just thinking out loud."
"Do go on."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."

"About that question — When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Recently — someone tripped over nothing and we all lost it. It felt like stealing."
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"Do go on."
They pull back half a step — not leaving, just... further.
"Do go on."
"What's this about? Three days ago. Someone dropped a whole basket of tubers and we just stood there laughing. It wasn't even funny. It was the standing there."
"Wait — what were we talking about?"
"Still on the last time you laughed."
"Wait — what were we talking about?"
"Like I said — we're still on the last time you laughed."
"Wait — what were we talking about?"
"We're going in circles — still on the last time you laughed. Ask me something else if you want."
"Can I ask you something else?"
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Could I show you something?"
You show them Cattail — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Do go on."
They hear you out, but something in them stays guarded.
"Do go on."
"I should get back to it."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They nod, already turning away.
"You told me about the stolen laugh — someone tripping over nothing. Have you stolen any more since?"
"Yes."
They nod. "Okay."
"Do go on."
Something in them stays shut, for now.
